episodes.196810: Line of storms ahead of a strong low pressure system produced a concentrated swath of 70-90 mph winds in northeast Kansas up to the Nebraska border, with just a few isolated wind gust reports elsewhere.
episodes.197008: A shortwave passed across the area, bringing widespread rain with over two inches falling in much of southeast Iowa. By afternoon weak instability developed, and when combined with robust available shear, was enough to produce isolated hail and damaging wind gusts. Storms organized into a QLCS in the evening and while hodographs were supportive of rotating updrafts and the potential for tornadoes, storms remained just elevated and prevented any further development.
episodes.197142: On the morning of October 30th, a longwave trough was situated over the Rockies, slowly pivoting east into the Great Plains. At the surface, a near stationary frontal zone extended from Minneapolis, southeast into the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. This brought the frontal zone through portions of southwest Iowa and southeast Nebraska. Scattered thunderstorms developed across north-central Kansas by 9:00am, moving northeast parallel to the surface front boundary. Through the late morning and early afternoon hours, these thunderstorms moved into southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa from Kansas while additional thunderstorms developed over these same area. Widespread heavy rain and lightning was observed, with isolated instances of severe hail east of Lincoln and south of Omaha. Just after 12 pm CDT, a bowing line segment developed in southeast Nebraska south of Highway 2. This line of storms brought destructive winds to the Falls City area, with a recorded wind gust of 90 mph at the Falls City ASOS, and widespread tree and structural damage reported in the town itself.
episodes.197176: A cold front moving through an unstable air mass produced strong thunderstorms over west half portions of Lake Superior on the 30th.
episodes.197370: A very warm and humid air mass remained in place across the Four State Region during the final week of October, ahead of an upper level trough and associated cold front that approached the area from the Southern Plains on October 30th. Low level moisture and associated instability increased across East Texas, North Louisiana, and Southern Arkansas ahead of the front during the afternoon of the 30th, with weak forcing ahead of the trough contributing to isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the region. One storm briefly became severe over Northern Bossier Parish in Northwest Louisiana, where damaging winds downed a tree just southwest of Plain Dealing. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed later in the evening through the day on the 31st, but did not become severe given the diminished instability.
episodes.197394: Thunderstorms developed near a boundary stretching from south central into northeast Kansas. Some of the storms intensified in severity across south central and southeast portions of the state. There were 60 to 70 mph winds reported along with up to half dollar sized hail. Some tree damage occurred.
episodes.197518: During the afternoon and evening hours of October 30th, storms produced widespread damaging wind gusts to portions of Missouri.

A swath of destructive straight line winds impacted portions of southeast Richardson County including Falls City. The Falls City ASOS measured a 91 miles per hour wind gust at 1:09 pm CDT, and again at 1:12 pm CDT. The ASOS lost power and stopped transmitting data at 1:15 pm CDT. Widespread tree damage was reported across Falls City with snow plows assisting in the removal of tree debris. Trees went through the roofs of two homes, and an additional house had a wall blown down as reported by law enforcement. A large factory in town lost approximately 3 to 4 thousand square feet of its roof. Powerlines were down across the southeast portion of the county, debris was strewn out across fields, and a school bus was reported to have been moved by the wind.
